title: St. Josaphat, Bishop and Martyr
subtitle: Memorial · Eph 4:1-7, 11-13; Jn 17:20-26 (or feria: Phlm 7-20; Lk 17:20-25)
text: St. Josaphat Kuntsevych, a Ruthenian monk who became archbishop of Polotsk, worked tirelessly to bring his Eastern Christian flock into full communion with Rome. In 1623 a mob opposed to that union killed him at Vitebsk. Today, pray for Christian unity and for the Church in Ukraine and Belarus.
imageAlt: In a dark forest clearing, a bearded bishop in grey robes lies wounded on the ground, supported by companions, while men armed with axes and clubs crowd around him.
credit: Józef Simmler, The Martyrdom of St. Josaphat Kuntsevych, c. 1861, National Museum in Warsaw. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
